correctness.rationale: The proof reduces unrestricted ellipsoids by averaging over S_n times coordinate swap using convex inversion, classifies all tight-spanning extreme potentials, derives all three quadratic branches and edge inverse coefficients, and proves the nine-order contact lower bound by exact positive convex mixture and Cauchy–Schwarz. For n>=10, the unique stationary subgradient multiplier has a negative component; convex separation of all three active branch gradients yields a strict common descent direction. Polynomial signs hold in every order. Exact rational independent calculations through n=500 and a rational n=10 witness corroborate but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: This answers a natural sharp stability question for Euclidean distortion under deleting a canonical perfect matching: the full biclique retains maximal distortion at arbitrary dimensions, yet the matching-deleted graph loses maximality at a precisely located integer transition. Three potential orbits and an elementary dimension-dependent negative contact coefficient explain the boundary. The exact variational formula may support future calculations for n>=10.
